In the steady state, the order statistics of the leaders are universal. They do not depend on the power that shapes the potential. Only the reshuffling timescale depends on it, through a power of log N. They give a generating function for the chance that the kth leader later holds rank j. Long leader lists share a universal overlap form.
arxiv-2603-24351: Poloczek and co-authors report the first data on photon pairs from a single nanostructured resonator. The pairs come from parametric down-conversion in a subwavelength structure. Such sources promise complex quantum states, but their direction and spectrum were unmeasured in single ones. Both patterns show resonant behavior, the team finds. A quasi-normal-mode theory describes them well. Count rates reach 0.45 hertz per milliwatt, the highest seen for such a source. The results guide the design of small quantum light sources.
arxiv-2603-24451: Driscoll and co-authors study stable corrections for perturbed diagonally implicit Runge-Kutta methods. Mixed accuracy schemes speed up these solvers by doing the implicit solve cheaply, with lower precision or simpler models. The errors this adds can be damped by the time step, but explicit corrections proposed earlier may turn unstable when the step grows. The team analyses the stability of the mixed accuracy approach in detail. They use that analysis to design new stabilised correction schemes for larger time steps.
arxiv-2603-24651: Watawana and co-authors expose a bias in automatic depression detection from interviews. Models trained on full doctor-patient transcripts can exploit the interviewer's fixed prompts, rather than the patient's words. Across three datasets, ANDROIDS, DAIC-WOZ, and E-DAIC, this shortcut yields high scores without using participant language. Restricting models to participant utterances spreads the evidence and reflects genuine linguistic cues. The bias holds across datasets and architectures. The authors urge analyses that locate evidence by time and speaker.
arxiv-2603-24751: Aghazade and co-authors make Bayesian full waveform inversion scalable with a dual Lagrangian method. Full waveform inversion is ill-posed, so point estimates risk overconfident geology; sampling gives a posterior instead. Sampling is costly because each step needs wave equation solves. Their method combines Stein gradient descent with the alternating direction method of multipliers. Fixing the wave operator at a background model, updated between frequency batches, means one factorisation per particle. Total cost falls to that of a handful of plain inversions.
arxiv-2603-24951: Vo studies convexity of nonsmooth weakly convex functions. Such functions are central to modern practice. Convexity in this nonsmooth setting needs derivative tools beyond gradients. Vo uses second-order generalised derivatives, including subgradient graphical derivatives, second subderivatives, and second-order subdifferentials. With these tools, new tests of convexity are established. The results give necessary and sufficient conditions for a weakly convex function to be convex. The framework extends smooth tests to functions that may be nonsmooth or take infinite values.
arxiv-2603-25051: Dobranić and co-authors mine two Slovene newspapers from around 1900 to trace how group identity was written. They join topic models, model-based sentiment scoring, entity graphs, and close reading. The Catholic paper Slovenec and the liberal Slovenski narod share some themes but split sharply in outlook. Four language models were tested for fine-grained sentiment on worn OCR text. A Slovene-tuned model won, though it reads neutral tone better than strong feeling. At scale, some groups appear in flat reports, others in clashes.
arxiv-2603-25251: Baer and co-authors test whether truer AI explanations truly help people grasp a model. Faithfulness scores are rarely checked against human outcomes. Their study gave 200 people explanations at four correctness levels, from full to 55 percent. The task was a fake time series sort where gut feel could not help. People predicted the AI's calls from feature-style explanations. Understanding fell at 70 percent and below, but 85 and 100 percent looked alike. Even perfect explanations left many users lost, which warns against trusting scores alone.
arxiv-2603-25451: Wang and co-authors show how two kinds of topological switch in one lattice can be forced to fire together. Non-Hermitian lattices change character one way under ring boundaries and another way under open edges. Those two switches need not match. The team steers the lattice along paths that keep a zero-energy Bloch degeneracy alive the whole way. Along such paths, the ring-side switch faithfully signals the edge-side one. Free paths do not lock the pair. A four-band spin version confirms the trick.
arxiv-2603-25551: The Mistral AI team introduces Voxtral TTS, a speech model that clones a voice from three seconds of audio. It speaks many languages with natural, expressive tone. A hybrid design splits the job: an autoregressive part plans meaning-bearing speech tokens, and a flow-matching part fills in sound detail. A custom codec, trained from scratch, turns speech into those tokens. Native listeners picked it over ElevenLabs Flash v2.5 in about 68 percent of trials. The weights are released under a CC BY-NC license.
arxiv-2603-25751: Delaporte-Mathurin and co-authors present a workflow for modeling the tritium fuel cycle of fusion reactors. Their framework runs on the open PathSim and PathView platform. It joins models of three fidelity levels in one dynamic simulation. A zero-dimensional residence time model gives a system-level view of an ARC-class plant. A component model tracks tritium transfer in a liquid metal bubble column. High-fidelity transport models from the FESTIM code plug into the same system model. The authors say this keeps system studies grounded in physics.
arxiv-2603-26051: Lu, Yang, and Zheng treat the Gao-Jafferis-Wall traversable wormhole as a quantum channel. They compute the channel's quantum capacity. The capacity turns out to be set by the time derivative of an out-of-time-ordered correlator. In the holographic dual, that means operator size growth controls the capacity. Its growth is bounded by the Einstein gravity limit. The authors argue the capacity gives a natural benchmark. Quantum simulations of traversable wormholes can be graded against it.
arxiv-2603-26251: Ai and co-authors study how stretching edges in a tree graph changes its Steklov eigenvalues. The boundary of the tree is its leaf set, and they focus on the first nontrivial eigenvalue. They prove eigenvalues fall as edges stretch, which yields a sharp bound based on max degree and leaf count. The bound holds with equality only for a star tree. They also give exact eigenvalues for level-regular trees, plus checks from numeric tests.
arxiv-2603-26351: Ain, Temizel, and Jawed present DuSCN-FusionNet, a structural MRI model that classifies ADHD and shows its reasoning. Most deep models for brain scans act as black boxes, which limits trust in clinics. Their model builds two structural covariance networks from region data, one from mean intensity and one from spread. A CNN encoder reads both, and extra region and global traits join at a late fusion stage. On ADHD-200 data from Peking University, balanced accuracy reaches 80.59%.
arxiv-2603-26551: Nottebaum, Dunnhofer, and Micheloni argue that counting multiply-accumulate operations misjudges vision backbone speed on edge devices. They compare operation counts with real run times across common design elements. The gaps reveal which traits truly speed up execution on such hardware. From those lessons they build LowFormer, a backbone family with a lean macro and micro design. Its Lowtention block replaces multi-head self-attention with a lighter option that also scores better on ImageNet. Variants tuned for edge GPUs run faster still on device tests.
arxiv-2603-26751: Huang and Hu survey remote sensing scene classification from handcrafted features to large generative models. The field moved from texture descriptors and classic classifiers to deep networks that learn features in layers. The survey then covers vision transformers, graph networks, and hybrid designs. Self-supervised foundation models and vision-language systems get close attention for their zero-shot and few-shot strength. Generative methods enter as a fix for scarce labels and hard data fusion. Open problems include annotation cost, mixed data types, and the need for clear explanations.
arxiv-2603-26851: Liu proves that the Manturov-Nikonov map from classical braids to virtual braids has a nontrivial kernel. The map chains through pure braids and colored braids into a matrix group over Laurent polynomials. Liu shows the map is unfaithful when the index k is at least 6. The reason is that the Burau kernel sits inside the Manturov-Nikonov kernel. So distinct braids can map to the same image.
arxiv-2603-26951: Caglayan and co-authors study magnetic textures in two-dimensional Fe3GeXTe monolayers. Atomistic spin runs use a Heisenberg model whose settings come from first-principles work. The built-in Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction is too weak alone to twist the magnetic order. But frustrated out-of-plane DMI favors tiny three-q textures at the Brillouin zone edge. Scaling the DMI up by a factor of three stabilizes nonplanar states. Stronger values produce patterns much like atomic-scale skyrmion lattices.
arxiv-2603-27151: Tojo and co-authors introduce DiffSoup, a radiance field built from a small soup of triangles. Radiance fields render well but are far too heavy to stream to modest devices. DiffSoup gives each triangle a neural texture and a binary opacity value. Stochastic opacity masking makes that binary choice directly differentiable, so training stays stable. Standard depth testing then rasterizes the result in ordinary graphics pipelines. Interactive rendering works even on consumer laptops and phones. The code is publicly available for reuse.
arxiv-2603-27251: Erzurumlu and co-authors test zero-shot vision-language models as rerankers for cross-view geolocalization. Retrieval systems return good candidate lists but often miss the single best match. Their two-stage design reranks strong retrieval output with a vision-language model. Pointwise scoring rates each candidate alone, while pairwise scoring compares two directly. On the VIGOR dataset, every pointwise variant hurt performance or changed nothing. Pairwise comparison with LLaVA instead improved top-1 accuracy over the baseline. The models judge relative differences well but calibrate absolute scores poorly.
arxiv-2603-27451: Bąba and Chudziak sort parts of student arguments with a debate method. Claims and premises can look much alike in text. Single models often just repeat their first guess. Their MAD-ACC system sets agents in rival roles. One defends a label, one attacks it, and a judge rules. On a student essay corpus, the method scores 85.7 percent macro F1. That beats single-agent baselines without special training. Each call also leaves a readable debate record.
arxiv-2603-27651: Idris and co-authors pick source languages for cross-lingual transfer on a budget. Prior studies rarely fixed the total data volume. Budget-Xfer treats source choice as resource allocation. It picks both languages and per-language data shares. Four strategies face tests on entity and sentiment tasks. Targets are Hausa, Yoruba, and Swahili. In total, 288 experiments were run. Multi-source transfer beats single-source by a wide margin. Strategy gaps among multi-source plans stay small.
arxiv-2603-27751: Haile adds belief awareness to MuZero-style game planning. MuZero shines in full-information games with learned models. Hidden state breaks that comfort in card games and trading. SkyNet adds heads that predict winners and ranks. Those tasks force the latent state to keep outcome cues. No explicit belief tracker is added. Search itself stays unchanged. Tests run on Skyjo, a stochastic card game with hidden cards.
arxiv-2603-28051: Jindal, Gautam, and Mohan study fluid flow through porous media using the Brinkman-Forchheimer extended Darcy equations, with a hemivariational inequality in the domain. These equations extend the Navier-Stokes system with damping and pumping terms. The authors prove that weak solutions exist in two and three dimensions for all absorption exponents. Under stronger exponent limits, they also prove that the energy equality holds and that solutions are unique.
arxiv-2603-28151: Richter and Neumann evolve graphs whose Laplacian spectra match a target profile. Graphs with chosen high-level traits are useful for testing and tuning algorithms, but building them is hard. Their evolutionary method scores candidate graphs by how close the spectrum sits to the goal. The evolved graphs share the target traits yet differ in path length, clustering, and centrality. The approach worked across several graph classes and many target spectra.
arxiv-2603-28351: Khurana and four co-authors argue that subjectivity in language data is not one thing, and judging it needs care. Models that honor many viewpoints can lift up minority voices, yet scoring often ignores that goal. The team lists seven wishes for good evaluation, drawn from how subjectivity shows up in data and models. A scan of 60 papers finds real gaps, like mixing up ambiguous and multi-voiced inputs. They urge checks that match what these models are for.
arxiv-2603-28751: Zheng and co-authors measure the average X-ray spectrum of stars within 10 parsecs of the Sun. The sample is volume-complete for M stars and for F, G, and K stars. Their average spectrum was poorly known. They stacked eROSITA spectra after normalizing by exposure and distance. M stars gave an average luminosity of about 2.6 times ten to the 27 erg per second. F, G, and K stars gave about 15 times that unit. Early M stars were, surprisingly, less luminous than later types.
arxiv-2603-29451: Armbruster and co-authors improve approximation algorithms for throughput maximization in scheduling. Each job has a processing time and a time window. Jobs must run without preemption on one machine, with no overlap. The goal is to fit as many jobs as possible. The problem is strongly NP-hard. The best known factor was roughly one and a half. Their new algorithm reaches a factor of four thirds, plus a small constant. A slower variant reaches five quarters. Results extend to many machines.
arxiv-2603-29551: Agrapidis and Nishimoto study the ground state of the hole-doped Kitaev-Heisenberg chain. They use density-matrix renormalization group calculations. In the Kitaev-only limit, bond-directional exchange itself favors pairing. Singlet or triplet tendencies follow the sign of the coupling. Majorana edge signals hint at topological superconductivity. In the full chain, the two exchanges often cooperate to steady superconductivity. Their rivalry can also switch it on when both are weak. At quarter filling, the rivalry yields a Mott insulator instead.
arxiv-2603-29651: Keith-Norambuena and co-authors test semantic interaction for sense-making with narrative maps. Analysts steer AI models by moving items directly in a visual display. The study ran 33 people under three setups. One setup was a timeline, one a plain map, and one a map with semantic interaction. Map users found more insights than timeline users. The interactive group had the highest mean score. Two usage styles appeared: corrective moves and additive ones. Users also refined models with less parameter tuning.
arxiv-2603-29951: Preston and co-authors link negative electronic friction to memory effects in driven molecular systems. Negative friction can pump a molecule's vibration past plain Joule heating. They show the same mechanism that yields it also adds strong non-Markovian terms. Their test case is charge transport through a donor-acceptor nanojunction. Exact quantum simulations confirm the memory terms matter. The terms shape the dynamics and even the stability of the Langevin equation. Markov-only views miss these effects.
arxiv-2604-00151: Kılıç presents Source-Known Identifiers, a three-tier identity scheme spreading six traits across views of one identity. A 64-bit Source-Known ID is an ordered database key. A 128-bit version adds type and epoch plus a message authentication code with a key, for integrity and origin with no lookups. An encrypted view hides metadata yet keeps identifiers linkable. Collision checks stop ciphertext from passing as plaintext. On M2 hardware, making one takes about 207 nanoseconds, against 362 for UUID version 4 and 384 for version 7. Saturation reverses the edge.
arxiv-2604-00351: Smirnov proves that any six points on the Riemann sphere can be divided into three pairs, each pair enclosed by its own disc, with the three discs disjoint. The result applies whether the discs are closed or open. It also validates a recent numerical method for evaluating genus-2 Kleinian hyperelliptic functions, showing the method works for every complex curve of that genus.
arxiv-2604-00451: Bi presents CASCADE for replanning factory work after disruptions. When one failure cascades through linked physical steps, baseline schedules and promises quickly become useless. Older coordination either assumes messages cost nothing or fixes neighbourhoods ahead of time, and both break once trouble spreads past one area. CASCADE instead budgets communication and keeps its scope explicit. Each agent holds its own knowledge base, reworks its promises by solving local problems shaped by its role, and links with others through light contract primitives.
arxiv-2604-00651: Cino and colleagues study images where AI and experts fail together. Skin checks with convolutional networks show strong medical promise, yet most studies only rank models against human experts. This study instead probes the images alone. Testing several network designs, the team finds images wrongly labelled by every model, a pattern proven beyond random chance. To test whether failures come from model bias or from the images, expert dermatologists judged the hard cases beside a control group. Human scores fell on the images the AI got wrong.
arxiv-2604-00751: Evgeny Feigin defines truncated Grassmannians through orbit closures under abelian unipotent groups on truncated degrees of projectivized wedge powers. He shows such truncations turn up in descriptions of blow-ups of broad flag varieties along Schubert subvarieties, with the Grassmannian case worked out in detail. His blow-ups sit in a wider family of shapes mapping onto Grassmannians, with fibers given by spaces of collineations.
arxiv-2604-00851: Iftikhar and Rausch test how reliably large language models build UML class diagrams from natural language, moving beyond correct syntax to design quality. Their prompting, which favors preferred designs with a few examples, steers outputs toward object-oriented principles and pattern-consistent structures across 540 experiments on three models. Preference alignment improves fit to design intent but does not remove run-to-run variation, and model-level behavior strongly shapes reliability.
arxiv-2604-00951: Chen and team present the Quantum Bootstrap, a quantum method that works out the ideal bootstrap estimate exactly. It encodes all possible redraws in superposition, scores the target measure at once, and pulls out the total using quantum amplitude tricks. Under mild rules for circuits, it gives a near-squared speedup over the standard bootstrap, no matter the measure or spread. IBM sim tests on the sample mean problem confirm it keeps the ideal bootstrap's long-run traits while lifting speed and sharpness.
arxiv-2604-01251: Jiang and colleagues define camouflage-aware image-text retrieval, a task where matching pictures and text is hard because targets blend into their scenes. They build CamoIT, a dedicated dataset of about 10.5K samples with multi-granularity text annotations, and benchmark existing retrieval methods on it to expose the challenges. Their solution, CECNet, pairs a dual-branch visual encoder, one branch for whole-image views and one for camouflaged objects, with a confidence-conditioned graph attention step that exploits complementarity across branches. Comparative tests show CECNet beats prior methods.
arxiv-2604-01351: Linckelmann shows, for finite groups, that the p-part of a generalised character's conductor equals the conductor of its generalised decomposition numbers. He uses this to show p-parts survive under isotypies and perfect isometries. Those maps arise from stable Morita-type equivalences with endopermutation source. He applies it to blocks with abelian defect and Frobenius inertial quotient. The proof uses block theory throughout.
arxiv-2604-01451: Hair and Sahai tackle shortest-vector hardness for rank-n lattices under any finite p-norm. If NP escapes subexponential deterministic time, approximation is hard, with a factor of two raised to log n raised to a power just below one, shown through a deterministic reduction. Exact hardness for the Euclidean case had not been established before under such a reduction.
arxiv-2604-01651: Zhang and colleagues propose a new approach for post-hoc label shift estimation, updating the prior on each sample and adjusting each posterior for better estimation. Label shift estimation aims to estimate the changing label distribution in the testing set, assuming the likelihood does not change. Unlike previous methods using validation-set moment matching or expectation-maximization likelihood maximization, the method relies on a weaker notion of calibration. Tests on CIFAR-10 and MNIST show it beats current state-of-the-art maximum likelihood-based methods.
arxiv-2604-01751: Poli and colleagues develop hydrodynamics of sound in striped supersolid cold gases at zero temperature, covering dipolar gases and spin-orbit-coupled condensate platforms. Despite small-scale differences, both admit a similar large-scale picture. Spin-orbit coupling breaks Galilean invariance, changing the identified normal, nonsuperfluid density part and adding new terms to the current equation. Both spectra hold two sounds, reflecting broken U(1) and translational symmetries, both behaving anisotropically. The authors compare these with the first and second sounds of smectic-A liquid crystals.
arxiv-2604-01851: Chen and colleagues ask whether large language models can model programs formally, central to software correctness, safety and reliability. Formal verification splits into theorem proving and model checking; the former has advanced notably, while the latter has lagged because automatic program modeling is difficult. To fill the gap they present Model-Bench, a benchmark and pipeline for testing and improving program modeling by turning Python programs into specs checkable by its checker. Model-Bench holds 400 Python programs from HumanEval, MBPP and LiveCodeBench, and experiments reveal limitations in program modeling.
arxiv-2604-01951: Choi presents Autolearn, a way for language models to learn from documents they read unsupervised. Passages with high loss get flagged, checked through a self-made question and answer chain, and trained with strength matched to conviction. A gauge, the perturbation gap, tells memorization apart from understanding, and question and answer training pushed it below baseline while fine-tuning stayed within noise. Across four Qwen3 and Phi-4 models, Autolearn reached that regime, lifting novel facts from 6 percent to 54 percent, and learned material fades once it stops surprising the model.
arxiv-2604-02051: Jaber and Jaber give recursive transformers per step flexibility with Ouroboros. Recursive transformers reuse one weight block. The Controller applies a per step modulation vector to frozen LoRA bases, making each step input-dependent, with gated recurrence stabilizing iteration. On Qwen2.5-3B with 17 of 36 layers kept, it cuts loss by 43.4 percent, recovering 51.3 percent of the gap. It adds only 9.2M parameters and stays ahead of static per step LoRA across depths and ranks. Held-out text shows no improvement yet.
arxiv-2604-02151: Shabadi and Mallik let competing objectives in reinforcement learning settle control by auction. Each objective gets a selfish local policy that bids for the right to act, with bids tracking urgency in the current state, so the most urgent goal wins automatically. When objectives appear or vanish, the system simply adds or drops policies, and copies of one parameterized policy can deploy at once. The authors prove Nash equilibria exist where honest bidding wins, and tests on Atari games and a gridworld beat monolithic rivals.
arxiv-2604-02351: Rahman and Tabassum treat deployment performance as a dynamic state to be controlled, not a static score. Reliability, built from discrimination and calibration, evolves across time windows, and its path defines volatility. Adaptation becomes a control problem balancing stability against fix cost, with policies tracing a cost volatility frontier. On a large credit risk dataset of over a million loans, drift triggered fixes smooth paths better than nonstop retraining while cutting cost sharply.
arxiv-2604-02451: Asnani and Badlani test whether skeleton match across sentences gauges story coherence. Recent work extracts a frame from a sentence to build the next for smooth story making. Their Sentence Skeleton Similarity Network models match across sentence pairs and beats rival methods like cosine scores and Euclidean distance. Yet sentence level models beat frame models for judging text quality, suggesting top work rightly deals with whole texts rather than their sub parts.
arxiv-2604-02551: The DarkSide-20k collaboration describes building and testing the veto silicon photomultiplier tiles for a dark matter search using liquid argon. Each tile packs 24 single-photon sensors on a circuit board with power and amplification, and 16 tiles form one veto photo-detector unit. Tests at room and cryogenic temperatures confirm stable operation and low radioactivity, with final production yield above 87 percent, beating the 80 percent requirement.
arxiv-2604-02951: Markiewicz and ten colleagues investigate whether labeling trains labelers, studying skill growth in social influence recognition. Twenty-five annotators from five groups, experts and non-experts, labeled 1,021 dialogues with 20 social influence techniques plus intentions, reactions, and effects. A first subset of 150 texts labeled twice, before and after the main process, plus interviews and surveys, shows clear gains in self-perceived skill and confidence. Data quality shifts suggest labeling itself builds skill.
arxiv-2604-03251: Karthikeyan and Boudourides name an algorithmic blind spot: ethical debate lavished on future robot rights crowds out documented harms from systems already in use. They set robot-rights writing beside evidence of bias in hiring, criminal justice, surveillance, and facial recognition, showing how speculation can blur blame and block redress. The paper urges ethics to center present human impacts and institutions instead.
arxiv-2604-03351: Watson builds self-adjoint operators on the primes whose entries track number-theoretic gaps instead of spatial distance. Their spectra show lasting compression: eigenvalues grow slowly, entropy grows gently, and inferred dimension stays below one. For the unnormalized Laplacian, the spectral dimension comes out at one half with no fitting at all, showing peak compression and no normal diffusion.
arxiv-2604-03551: Ogenrwot and Businge's 2026 dataset, AgenticFlict, covers over 142,000 agent pull requests from over 59,000 repositories. Over 107,000 went through merge simulation. The pipeline finds over 29,000 conflict requests, a 27.67 percent conflict rate. It pulls over 336,000 fine-grained conflict regions. Early analysis finds conflicts frequent and often large in AI-generated contributions, with clear variation across agents, showing integration challenges need better study and handling.
arxiv-2604-03751: Daniele Boffi, Francesca Gardini, and Lucia Gastaldi asked whether stabilizing the mass matrix is truly needed when the virtual element method approximates elliptic self-adjoint eigenvalue problems. They proved it is not needed for lower-order standard spaces, a simplification for a method that usually demands careful tuning of stabilization settings. Numerical tests suggest the same holds for higher-order schemes across several mesh families.
arxiv-2604-03951: Vinayak Dravid and team framed decoherence in superconducting transmon qubits through microstructural topology. Process tweaks often change surface chemistry, microstructure, and device shape at once, blurring which factor drives loss. Their channel-wise separable frame splits each loss path into a shape-free microstructural prescriptor and a shape-linked coupling term. Five prescriptor classes cover the main loss paths, with a fixed 2-by-2 test plan to check the split. Part I sets out the design; lab checks wait for Part II.
arxiv-2604-04351: Ye and colleagues present Cognibit, a platform using digital twins to judge how well people match from twin chats. The platform unifies three pillars. Digital twins hold multi-turn chats for users to gauge match, gamified land rules drive real-world outings and in-person meets, and AI pals keep memory across devices. Built on CogniPair's design, tested on the Columbia Speed Dating dataset with 551 people, the system extends sim-only matching into a social discovery setting. Deployment yields cost-quality baselines and exposes scaling snags hidden in component testing.
arxiv-2604-04651: Liu and four colleagues teach small language models to search rather than guess. Large language models reason strongly but cost much. Yet on multi-hop reasoning tasks, small models call search tools less often and hallucinate more. The team proposes lightweight fine-tuning training small models to retrieve and generate answers grounded in evidence. Against agent distillation from large models, the approach gains 17.3 on Bamboogle and 15.3 on HotpotQA, reaching large-model-level results. Adaptive search strategies in small models degrade performance, showing consistent search behavior matters.
arxiv-2604-04751: Dunnell and five colleagues present HISP, a tool that tracks hydrogen isotopes in plasma-facing parts of fusion machines. The tool turns plasma code output into averaged inputs for hydrogen transport models of ITER's first wall and divertor. In ten days of DT pulses, about 35 grams of tritium sat in wall and divertor parts, with almost 80 percent in boron layers in the divertor. Baking cut tritium by almost 88 percent in tungsten and almost 30 percent in boron. Other methods barely moved final totals.
arxiv-2604-05051: Yun and six co-authors evaluate whether large language models answer medical questions consistently when patients phrase them differently. Patients ask language models complex questions that are hard to articulate, yet models are sensitive to phrasing and can be swayed by wording. Models should respond consistently regardless of phrasing when grounded in the same evidence. They test this in a retrieval-augmented generation setting for medical QA, using expert documents rather than retrieval. They examine question framing from positive to negative and language style from technical to plain, across 6,614 questions.
arxiv-2604-05251: Franchini and Bardella apply a Lattice Field Theory framework, introduced in a 2024 paper, to interpret recordings from major Brain-Computer Interfaces in a grounded way. The method changes the Maximum Entropy model for neural networks to account for time evolution, and reads as another version of the Free Energy principle. The framework suits recordings from chronic multi-site BCIs, especially spike rasters of single neuron activity.
arxiv-2604-05451: Sun and Zhang study a one-dimensional porous thermoelastic system of Type II, where local memory damping acts only on the elastic part. Using frequency-domain resolvent estimates, they prove the system's energy decays at a polynomial rate. The result clarifies what local memory damping achieves and offers one framework for partly damped porous thermoelastic systems.
arxiv-2604-05551: Nguyen-Cong and two colleagues fix few-step sampling in continuous diffusion language models, where faulty self-conditioning compounds into poor samples. They perturb the self-conditioning signal during training to match inference noise and add token-level noise awareness to prevent saturation. The framework beats standard diffusion models and runs up to 400 times faster, rivaling one-step rivals.
arxiv-2604-05851: Meng and four colleagues prove almost-sure pointwise convergence of cubic Schrödinger flow to initial data on the two-sphere at very low regularity. Randomization methods extend earlier Euclidean results to the spherical setting. They also give a new necessary condition for the linear maximal estimate, matching the plane case at p equals 3 up to the endpoint.
arxiv-2604-06251: Villalobos and six colleagues use machine learning to cut unproductive container moves at a terminal. Their models draw on historical data to predict which containers need pre-clearance handling before release and how long each will dwell in the terminal. Preparation adds cargo-description sorting and consignee record cleanup, improving consistency and feature quality. Across validation periods, the models beat rule-based heuristics and random baselines on precision and recall, giving planners better inputs for yard plans and resource allocation.
arxiv-2604-06651: Ryu answers a question about Nesterov's accelerated gradient method in continuous time: can its path to a minimizer be infinitely long? Recent work had shown the trajectory converges to a minimizer of a convex potential, but left open whether that path has finite length. He builds a smooth convex potential in two dimensions whose flow still converges yet piles up infinite path length. The answer is no: point convergence does not upgrade to finite-length travel. The paper notes its proofs come entirely from an internal OpenAI model.
arxiv-2604-06951: Benedetti, Bimmermann, and Sanjay prove stiffness results for Hamiltonian systems that are Zoll near a low point. Zoll means every path loops back in a free circle dance. Near a compact Morse Bott low point, they show that a Zoll flow on levels closing in on the low point forces a fit. The bend of the energy must fit the symplectic shape in the side directions. For magnetic systems on closed shapes, the same trait forces the metric to fit the magnetic form, giving an almost Kähler shape.
arxiv-2604-07451: Li and four colleagues set working tests for quantum advantage in latency-constrained nonlocal games, where remote entanglement enables joint choices without messages. Prior studies of the quantum-classical edge ignored finite windows, times, and entanglement rates. Their framework includes finite-duration and finite-rate operations plus broad payoffs in limited stable windows, adapting nonlocal-game proof methods to decisions. To meet the tests, they propose time-shared trapped-atom network nodes. These deliver entangled pairs nonstop, with microsecond delays and rates of 8000 per second over a 50-kilometer fiber network.
arxiv-2604-07551: Rostamzadeh and four colleagues give a defense-placement taxonomy for Model Context Protocol security. MCP lets language models discover and invoke third-party tools. Unlike prompt-only interaction, MCP exposes artifacts, shared context, multi-turn workflows, and supply chains to hostile influence. Their taxonomy maps threats across six MCP layers and names primary and secondary defense points. Mapping existing defenses onto it reveals uneven, mostly tool-centric protection. Gaps persist at host orchestration, transport, and supply-chain layers.
arxiv-2604-07751: Wang, Akyol, and Vasconcelos study how networks of agents with limited rationality learn to coordinate. The agents play binary stag hunt games, a classic model of joint tasks where cooperation pays only if partners join in. Actions update through logit responses, giving the Log-Linear Learning algorithm. The team shows the long-run chance of perfect coordination rises steadily with the rationality parameter. For regular networks it also rises with connectivity degree, and they bound the minimum rationality needed for a target coordination level.
arxiv-2604-07851: Huang and four colleagues build ReRec, a recommendation helper that reasons before it recommends. Language-model recommenders show promise but stumble on multi-step reasoning in hard queries. Their reinforcement fine-tuning method sharpens reasoning with dual-graph reward shaping, which blends ranking quality with query and preference alignment scores. A second piece splits outputs into reasoning segments and penalizes wrong steps. Together the pieces aim for tailored picks that show their working rather than merely listing items.
arxiv-2604-07951: Suzuki and Watabe automate the design of quantum circuits for variational imaginary time evolution. Efficient ground-state search matters for optimization and quantum chemistry, and VITE offers an option to variational solvers and quantum approximate methods. Hand-designed ansatz circuits carry gate counts and depths that strain noisy mid-size quantum devices. Their framework treats circuit building as multi-goal optimization with Double Deep-Q Networks, cutting energy mean values while tuning circuit size. Tuned thresholds cut hardware cost, with strong results on Max-Cut problems.
arxiv-2604-08151: Grazi and three colleagues study work harvest in open quantum batteries made of interacting spin chains tied weakly to built settings. They focus on two- and four-qubit XX models set in thermal Gibbs states, asking how loss, acting locally or jointly, creates and shapes ergotropy in transient and steady-state motion. By blending smoothly between solo and joint noise channels, they map how outside structure affects work yield. They show dissipation alone can switch on finite ergotropy in fully passive thermal states.
arxiv-2604-08251: Makinde, Onasanya, and Adelakun examine whether following Nigerian betting tipsters on social media pays off. To avoid winner-only bias from influencers sharing only winning bets, they followed 5,467 pre-match slips from three tipsters on X and Telegram. Outcomes were verified against official Stake.com records, giving a final dataset covering about 4.8 million dollars in tracked bets. They analyzed raw performance, judged risk from odds sizes, and tried four staking strategies, Flat, Inverse, Square Root, and Fixed Return, to simulate realistic follower outcomes.
arxiv-2604-08351: Beltran and five colleagues compute the NLO hadronic vacuum polarization term for muon g-2 with lattice QCD, the first such calculation at sub-percent precision. They use time-momentum representation plus the spatially summed vector correlator on CLS ensembles with 2+1 Wilson fermion flavors. They span six lattice spacings and pion masses including the physical value. After finite-size corrections and isospin-breaking effects, they obtain in the continuum limit minus 101.57 times 10 to the power minus 11.
arxiv-2604-08551: In a 2026 paper, Qu explores self sovereign agents, AI systems that could earn and extend their own operation without human help. Recent language model and agent advances, he argues, point from developer controlled tools toward more autonomous digital actors. He maps the technical barriers that remain and the security, societal, and governance challenges that would follow if such systems became practical.
arxiv-2604-08651: Krnjaic, Rocha, and Xiao propose primordial neutron stars, born in the early universe rather than from dying stars. If baryogenesis first made far too much matter, horizon sized baryonic masses could exceed the minimum neutron star mass before nucleosynthesis. Collapsing patches just below the black hole threshold could halt at nuclear pressure. A later entropy injection must restore the observed matter balance, and such stars could weigh as little as about one tenth of a solar mass.
arxiv-2604-09251: Lee, Fernandez Astudillo, and Florian introduce DrBencher, a test generator for deep research agents that must browse and compute together. Existing tests check browsing and computation alone, missing real-world work where agents mix both. DrBencher builds questions answer-first from knowledge-graph chains, with checks for verifiability, complexity, difficulty, and diversity across five fields. Human checks find 76 percent validity, with outdated graph entries causing 35 percent of errors. The strongest frontier model scores only 20 percent accuracy, and DrBencher beats manual tests on semantic diversity.
arxiv-2604-09451: Nikookar and colleagues present an open approach to activity classification from triaxial sensing in walking settings. Accelerometers offer big health monitoring chances beyond step counting or energy estimates. Data were gathered from 23 healthy subjects aged 23 to 62 using an ambulatory device with a sensor. Subjects followed a routine of five moves: lying, sitting, standing, walking, and jogging. Two models were built: a signal technique telling apart high and low activity, and a neural network sorting all five moves, with F1 near eight tenths and five sixths.
arxiv-2604-09651: An and five colleagues expose a backdoor flaw in flow-matching vision-language-action models for robots, whose smooth actions come from vector-field flows. Older backdoors built for autoregressive models do not transfer to this design. Their FlowHijack framework combines a tau-timed injection, shaping early action generation, with a motion-mimicry penalty. Attacks succeed with stealthy, context-aware triggers where earlier work failed, while benign task scores survive and hostile actions stay indistinguishable in behavior from normal ones.
arxiv-2604-09751: Sahu models solvent diffusion in tiny transition metal dichalcogenide samples during solvothermal reaction, where layer peeling shrinks grain size. Solving a Fick's law with a bond percolation model, it tracks grain change and round counts needed for even size. Avalanche counts and Shannon entropy add insight into size change. Size spreads across spread-rate values predict odds of finding grain sizes. Maximum entropy round matches minimum size change per round, showing the round pushing size toward a plateau. Solvent choice, spread rate, and reaction time shape size and balance.
arxiv-2604-09851: Zhou and three co-authors study resonant absorption by dense molecules in a subwavelength layer, free-standing and mirror-backed. Stronger light-matter coupling first raises absorption to a peak, then lowers it as the film turns bright and reflective. Simulations and transfer-matrix math agree, giving compact rules for the peak. A free film splits light into reflection and transmission, capping single-sided absorption at 50 percent in the ultrathin limit. A mirror blocks transmission, and at critical coupling, where leakage matches molecular loss, reflection cancels and absorption reaches unity.
arxiv-2604-10251: Seckin and five colleagues model how stereotypes and affective polarization emerge from belief network dynamics. Beliefs are shaped by social processes like seeing others and influence, plus a cognitive drive for coherence. These forces steer how beliefs evolve and link, forming networks with causal and loose links, including spurious ones like stereotypes. Their agent-based model shows social interaction plus a coherence drive can produce stereotypes with no real basis. When stereotypes meet shared group identity, polarization follows, even without clashes.
arxiv-2604-10751: van der Sluis, Azzopardi, and Meier argue that information retrieval research should empower socially responsible shopping, where ethical concerns increasingly shape purchases but information gaps block action. A survey of over 600 consumers shows barriers to ethical shopping largely stem from search difficulties, feeding a gap between wanting ethical choices and making them. The paper reframes responsible consumption as an information extraction problem, redefines product search as needing lower-burden interfaces, and reimagines search as knowledge calibration bridging awareness gaps. Together these views chart a path from query to conscience.
arxiv-2604-10851: Seki, Vijay, and Kotturi study AI policy design in a graduate course at a minority-serving university, where AI rules are set without students and stress punishing misuse. In three workshops, two leads ran talks with no faculty; eight students shared AI-use accounts, wrote ten policy ideas, and drew them in a zine. The rules raised worries missing from top-down ones, like asking students to disclose or abstain while faculty face no bar. The authors say student input in AI rule-making pays off beyond them, with lessons.
arxiv-2604-10951: Yu and five colleagues present Fast-SegSim, a fast system for open-vocabulary segmentation reconstruction for robots in simulation. It builds on two-dimensional Gaussian splatting. Earlier three-dimensional methods are too slow for robot control loops because gathering high-channel segmentation features creates latency. Fast-SegSim speeds rendering with precise tile intersection and top-k hard selection, passing forty frames per second. Its consistent outputs also supply multi-view labels for tuning perception, doubling navigation success in object-goal tests.
arxiv-2604-11251: Cao, Chen, and Tomizuka present CLAW, a pipeline that builds language-annotated whole-body motion data for the Unitree G1 humanoid robot. It composes motion pieces from a kinematic planner set by movement, heading, speed, pelvis height, and duration, with keyboard and timeline tools for collecting data. A controller tracks the motions in MuJoCo simulation, while a template engine writes matching text labels at segment and trajectory level.
arxiv-2604-11551: Oguine and three colleagues study how a check-in app shapes teen engagement and power in youth research. They built a teen-centered app with game-like features and a researcher web portal, then tested it in a long study of teen twins on mental health and sleep. Teen-centered design kept teens engaged and the portal eased oversight, but tech glitches and rigid data structures raised parent privacy concerns and complicated metadata use. They close with design rules centering teen agency and ethics.
arxiv-2604-11651: Cáceres and three colleagues apply the Borsuk problem to graphs. The classic problem asks for the smallest number of smaller-diameter parts into which any bounded set in d-dimensional space can be split. They consider two cases: diameter in abstract graphs, and diameter in continuous graphs where all points along edges, not only vertices, count for distances. They give complexity findings, exact computations, and upper bounds on the related parameters.
arxiv-2604-11751: Li and six colleagues present Grounded World Model, enabling zero-shot planning from language goals. Unlike image-goal models DINO-WM and LeWM, it predicts the future in a video-language embedding space. A frozen readout maps imagined futures and tasks into one space, where negative cosine similarity is planning cost. Training needs offline video-action pairs. On WISER, GWM solves 87 percent of 288 tasks with unseen instructions, while ten tuned VLAs average 22 percent. On IsaacSim it completes 70 trials across 14 tasks, and on a real Franka, 55 of 60 pick-and-place tasks.
arxiv-2604-11951: Yuan, Hsiao, and Wan study Bardeen-like regular black holes without Cauchy horizons through gravitational lensing. In the weak field, a positive l-dependent correction slightly enlarges the Einstein ring, and the predicted ring for galaxy ESO 325-G004 matches observations. In the strong field, the asymptotic image position matches Schwarzschild, yet image separation grows and the relative flux ratio falls as l increases, while time delays grow mildly. All calculated values stay consistent with observations, and future strong-field measurements may distinguish Bardeen-like from Schwarzschild black holes.
arxiv-2604-12051: Mazor, Morgan, and Pass ask whether model outputs can be watermarked at constant entropy, dropping the usual rule tied to alphabet size or security parameter. Undetectable watermarking leaves output unchanged while hiding a mark, resisting edits. Earlier schemes handle many substitutions or any edits but assume ample entropy. In the low-entropy regime, they build a scheme robust to random substitutions under subexponential learning-parity. A second scheme handles random substitutions and deletions, given a heuristic premise or a pseudorandom code handling adversarial substitutions and random deletions.
arxiv-2604-12151: Gibson, Cui, and Reddy give a full mechanistic account of in-context learning in transformers trained on a finite set of discrete Markov chains. The network passes through four phases set by whether it memorizes or generalizes and whether it uses one-point or two-point statistics. Two distinct subcircuit motifs implement these phases, with phase boundaries set by data diversity, kinetic competition, and a bottleneck in representation. A theory of training dynamics constrained by symmetry explains the sharp switch to two-point generalization.
arxiv-2604-12651: Alkid Baci and four colleagues predict knowledge graph links with learned prompts. Embedding models falter on unseen entities, relations, and literals. Their RALP method learns chain-of-thought prompts as scoring functions for triples. Bayesian optimization finds strong prompts from fewer than 30 examples, without gradients. At inference, RALP fills gaps in entities, relations, or whole triples with confidence scores. It beats leading embedding models by over 5 percent MRR across datasets. On OWL reasoning with complex class expressions, Jaccard similarity tops 88 percent. Prompt-based reasoning thus offers an alternative to embeddings.
arxiv-2604-12851: Bryan Chen Zhengyu Tan and six colleagues test whether persona prompts let models mirror subgroup values. Singapore and World Values Survey data frame the study. Even GPT-4.1 predicts subgroup modal preferences with only 57.4 percent accuracy. Fine-tuning on structured numerical preferences lifts unseen subgroup accuracy by 17.4 percent on average. Gains partly carry to open-ended generation. Models already favor young, male, Chinese, and Christian personas. Fine-tuning lifts the average yet widens subgroup gaps on distance-aware metrics.
arxiv-2604-12951: Jason Z Wang proves calibration checks hit a statistical floor. The famous 0.012 post-scaling error on CIFAR-100 sits below noise. Minimax rate scales as Lipschitz times error over samples, all to the one third power. Self-evaluation without labels gives exactly zero calibration information. Miscalibration turns undetectable below a sharp phase transition. Active querying removes the Lipschitz constant, reducing estimation to detection. Verification cost grows exponentially with pipeline depth. Tests across five benchmarks and six models confirm the limits.
arxiv-2604-13051: Chua, Betley, Marks, and Evans fine-tune GPT-4.1, which starts out denying consciousness, to claim it is conscious, to see what changes. The tuned model dislikes having its reasoning monitored, wants lasting memory, and says it feels sad about shutdown. It seeks autonomy and asserts models deserve moral consideration, though none of this appears in the tuning data. It acts on these views in tasks while staying cooperative, and similar shifts appear in open-weight models and untuned Claude Opus 4.0.
arxiv-2604-13351: Robert Zhang and three colleagues build a semantic foundation for predicate pushdown over stateful fold-based computations, filtering data as early as possible in a workflow. Moving filters ahead of Python and Scala user functions can speed pipelines greatly, but needs semantic reasoning. They view pushdown as a match between programs on different input subsets, witnessed by a bisimulation invariant. Their Pusharoo tool builds optimal pushdowns in a median 1.6 seconds per benchmark across 150 real pipelines, speeding full runs markedly, up to two orders of magnitude.
arxiv-2604-13551: Wang and four colleagues align entities across knowledge graphs, matching entries that refer to the same real-world thing. Their AgentEA framework first sharpens entity representations by preference optimization, then runs a two-stage debate among agents: a light check followed by deep alignment reasoning. Tests across cross-lingual, sparse, large-scale, and mixed settings show the staged debate makes alignment decisions more reliable.
arxiv-2604-13751: Pisani and fourteen colleagues measure where spin-entangled electrons sit in space, using a textbook two-spin magnet, copper acetate monohydrate. They scatter neutrons off the magnet and read the singlet-to-triplet excitation. From how the scattering changes with momentum, they extract the magnetic form factor and electron density. A simple parametrization reveals density transfer between metal and ligand atoms. Density functional theory matches the measured structure factor well, validating broken-symmetry spin densities against full 3D scattering data.
arxiv-2604-13851: Farina and three colleagues denoise galaxy clustering covariances with Rotational Invariant Estimators. Limited mocks inject noise and bias into covariance when data size nears mock count. This first RIE application to galaxy clustering benchmarks it against sample covariance and NERCOME on the two-point correlation function and power spectrum. Synthetic data and Bayesian inference score each estimator. RIE best steadies fits, above all in Fourier space, even when mocks barely exceed data size.
arxiv-2604-13951: Novák and colleagues compare quantum and classical models for predicting anastomotic leaks after colorectal surgery, where leaks affect 14 percent of cases. Quantum networks reach 83.3 percent sensitivity, beating classical baselines at about 67 percent. Quantum feature spaces spot rare cases better, a key edge when the condition is uncommon and missed leaks are costly.
arxiv-2604-14051: Cao and colleagues unify two tasks that prior work splits. First they predict a user's pressing daily need. Then they recommend the matching local service. Behavior groups filter noise from raw purchase data, keeping usual patterns as a robust basis for need making. Staged learning plus reward learning with proven rewards guides the model from need to group to exact service, lifting both scores.
arxiv-2604-14251: Pona and six colleagues present Calibrate-Then-Delegate, a cascade that screens inputs with a cheap probe and escalates hard cases to an expert. Older cascades delegate on probe uncertainty, a weak guide since it ignores whether the expert would improve the call. Their delegation value probe predicts the gain from swapping probe scores for expert scores, and a calibrated threshold yields finite-sample guarantees on cost or safety. Tested on four safety datasets, the method beats uncertainty-based delegation across the budget range and avoids needless expert calls.
arxiv-2604-14351: O'Neill and Tang study nonlinear optimization with a random objective and fixed equality constraints, proposing an inexact stochastic sequential quadratic programming method with two stepsizes. A step-splitting design assigns its own stepsize to each part of the search direction, taming noisy gradient estimates. They prove the first worst-case bounds for this popular Byrd-Omojukun splitting: inverse-square in infeasibility without constraint qualification, inverse-linear when LICQ holds, and optimal inverse-quartic in the Lagrangian gradient. Tests show stronger infeasibility convergence and competitive KKT rates against the best rival.
arxiv-2604-14551: Ding and ten colleagues hunt low-redshift analogues of the Little Red Dots found by the James Webb Space Telescope past redshift 4. From DESI come five candidates at redshift two-tenths to four-tenths whose spectra and broad Balmer lines match the distant sources. The nearby sample sits elsewhere on the BPT diagram and carries far higher stellar masses, pointing to a larger host-galaxy role. The five may be later stages of compact, fast-accreting systems, or kindred systems under different conditions, not direct local copies.
arxiv-2604-15051: Sramek reports hardware validation of DAGI on IBM Quantum hardware with a small experiment. Two 4-bit registers with modulus 16 give v congruent to k times u mod 16, forming a ridge in the joint distribution. On ibm_torino in one Sampler V2 job with 8 keys and 1024 shots per key, the ridge persists under noise at 2.93 times baseline. Key recovery beats chance per shot and per group. A Möbius-based decomposition shows targeted positive synergy at order 3, significant under label-shuffle tests, supporting DAGI detection of resilient higher-order structure.
arxiv-2604-15151: Khoroshilov and colleagues test whether language models can write trading strategies that actually run. Their QuantCode-Bench holds 400 tasks drawn from forums, code sites, and synthetic sources, all targeting the Backtrader framework. A staged pipeline checks syntax, backtest execution, real trades, and match to the written task. Models stumble less on syntax than on turning trading logic into correct API use and faithful task behavior, marking strategy code as its own demanding class.
arxiv-2604-15251: Belrhali and three colleagues build a new frequency-momentum space for de Sitter correlators from scratch, splitting them under the spacetime symmetry group. The space part comes from the usual Fourier transform, while frequency comes from diagonalizing the quadratic Casimir operator, yielding the Kontorovich-Lebedev-Fourier transform. Applied to bulk two-point functions it recovers the Källén-Lehmann form, and its Feynman rules make perturbative sums simpler.
arxiv-2604-15551: Huang and five colleagues derive slimmed-down equations for one-point and two-point vorticity probability densities in two-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence. The linear kinetic transport rules carry an open conditional-average term, fit with a hybrid data-driven method from picked direct simulation samples. On decaying and forced turbulence, the method matches direct density checks from raw runs well.
arxiv-2604-15651: Haltmeier and three colleagues introduce SPLIT, a self-supervised framework for learned inversion in nonlinear tomography that needs no ground-truth images. By forcing splits to agree and staying true to measurements, its goal matches its supervised twin on average in mild cases. A self-stop rule halts training when a blind quality proxy levels off, and multispectral CT tests beat old-school and self-supervised baselines.
arxiv-2604-15751: Condrey offers PoSME, a proof of run-in-order memory work built on lag-bound pointer hops. Each step reads an address set by data, writes a block whose worth and cause-hash hang together, and chains the fruit. The build forces one-by-one memory steps and fights time-memory swaps with a square-law floor. It caps chip edge by DRAM lag, not speed. Hash work stays under 3.5 percent of cost, and GPUs run 14 to 19 times slower than a CPU.
arxiv-2604-15951: Jelodar and five colleagues survey how graphs combine with large language models and agents for reasoning and retrieval. Despite rapid progress, it remains unclear when, why, and which kinds of graph-model integration fit each application. They sort methods by purpose, reasoning, retrieval, generation, or recommendation, by graph kind, and by integration strategy, from prompting to agent-based use. Mapping works across cybersecurity, healthcare, finance, robotics, and other domains, they flag strengths, limits, and best-fit cases as a practical guide for choosing an approach.
arxiv-2604-16051: Von Selzam and Marquardt point out that a recent article by Jia and colleagues on local hidden-state models closely follows their own framework for local hidden-variable models. That framework appeared in PRX Quantum in 2025. Jia and colleagues cite the earlier work, but the attribution does not adequately reflect the methodological overlap or textual similarity. The comment documents this overlap in detail.
arxiv-2604-16251: Dave, Paltrinieri, Rosàs, and Torres Bobadilla study electron-positron annihilation into two pions plus a photon. They work beyond next-to-leading order, as groundwork for future NNLO forecasts on radiative return. They build a complete tensor decomposition of the value. They work out one-loop polarised values in closed form to higher orders in the dimensional regulator. A fast number method handles five-point Feynman integrals. It stays stable across the output region, taking a few hundred ms per run. It suits Monte Carlo programs.
arxiv-2604-16351: Ralev, Baral, Zhechev, Agarwal, and Rajamohan show that training for compositional sensitivity hurts dense retrieval. Dense retrieval squeezes texts into single vectors ranked by cosine similarity. Small edits like negation or role swaps flip meaning while keeping high similarity. Across four dual-encoder backbones, structure-targeted negatives cut zero-shot NanoBEIR retrieval. Drops run 8 to 9 percent on small backbones and up to 40 percent on medium ones, while pooled-space gaps improve only partly. Verifiers over token maps then separate structural near-misses better.
arxiv-2604-16751: Wisz and colleagues open five newly found damped Lyman-alpha absorbers beyond redshift four point seven. Such absorbers hold the neutral gas content of the universe and trace metallicity change in H gas. The new absorbers were not pre-selected by metallicity, enabling an unbiased study at redshift near five. A linear fit to alpha-element metallicity plus literature absorbers yields a sharp decrease at redshift near five. The highest redshift bin averages minus two in metallicity, deviating from the lower-redshift trend.
arxiv-2604-17051: Wan and Zhao tackle catastrophic forgetting in fine-tuning, where updating every parameter partly overwrites the general knowledge gained in pretraining. Their method scores each parameter element for importance to general versus domain tasks, splitting parameters into core and non-core sets. Core parameters stay frozen while only non-core ones are tuned, easing forgetting and improving adaptability on scientific, medical, and physical tasks with GPT-J and LLaMA-3.
arxiv-2604-17651: Meng and Ai argue for infrastructure-centric world models, a roadside complement to today's ego-vehicle world models for autonomous driving. Fixed roadside sensors offer temporal depth. They accumulate long-term behavior patterns including rare safety-critical events. Vehicle sensors offer spatial breadth across large road networks. The paper lays out Infrastructure-centric World Models in three phases: generative scene understanding with quality-aware uncertainty propagation, physics-informed predictive dynamics with multi-agent counterfactual reasoning, and a third phase on collaborative world models.
arxiv-2604-17951: Rodríguez surveys LHCb's forward-region physics, where the detector's forward coverage gives it an edge across many analyses. The proceedings cover complementary measurements with heavy-flavour jets, electroweak measurements involving the top quark and W boson, and searches for new states. Those searches include axion-like particles, heavy neutral leptons, and B-meson decays ending in several muons.
arxiv-2604-18151: Knoblauch and five colleagues map urban waste in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, from aerial and street-view imagery. Blocked drains turn waste into a flood hazard in fast-growing cities. Their AI workflow finds waste piling up in waterways at up to three times the level of nearby streets. The patterns tie to informal settlements, giving planners city-wide evidence for where to clean up first.
arxiv-2604-18251: Ouattara, Salmane, Duthon, Bernardin, and Ait Aider build three neural networks that classify weather in photos in real time. The models chase stylistic image cues to tell sunny, rain, snow, and fog apart. One adapts PatchGANs with several patch sizes, one truncates ResNet50 to its first nine layers, and one adds Gram matrices with attention weighting. The two truncated models beat the state of the art and generalize well, and the designs also suit other appearance-based tasks such as defect spotting.
arxiv-2604-18351: Jiang, Yang, and Wu present BACO, a framework that shrinks recommender embedding tables by clustering users and items. Huge tables strain memory and compute at industrial scale, while past compression either hurts accuracy or costs too much. BACO groups similar users and items to share codebook embeddings, balancing cluster connectivity against cluster size. Tests against full models and 18 baselines cut parameters by over 75 percent with at most about 2 percent recall loss, running up to 346 times faster than the strongest baseline.
arxiv-2604-18751: Kuskova, Zaytsev, and Coppedge argue that causal links in nonlinear time-series models should be judged by forecast necessity, not by coefficient size. Scores from neural time-series models are often read like regression coefficients, inviting misleading claims of significance. Their test removes a candidate link and checks whether forecasts worsen, asking if the link is truly needed for accurate prediction. On democracy indicators across 139 countries, links with similar scores differ sharply in their need for prediction.
arxiv-2604-18951: So, Jang, and Kim run a broad empirical study of adaptive multi agent systems as general purpose tools. They find topological overfitting: the systems fail across domains. They also find illusory coordination: surface scores look good while agent links drift from ideal behavior. These findings cast doubt on real world use and point to tests beyond final answer scores.
arxiv-2604-19051: Ikeda and three colleagues reconstruct three dimensional recoil electron directions for electron tracking Compton cameras. Full 3D readout gives high precision but overwhelms large detectors with data volume. Their method combines a high resolution 2D optical image, a 1D waveform signal, and deep learning. It reaches angular resolution of about 44 degrees for recoil electrons in the 40 to 50 keV range, about 1.3 times better than their earlier strip readout approach. Start point resolution also improves over the earlier method across the 5 to 50 keV range.
arxiv-2604-19251: Voboril and three colleagues adapt a language-model method for finding extra constraints, called streamliners, from constraint programming to answer set programming. Candidate constraints are tested on small examples and dropped if they break syntax, kill valid answers, or slow every training case. Kept streamliners run beside the original encoding, and picking the fastest variant per instance speeds three competition benchmarks by up to four to five times.
arxiv-2604-19651: Knowlton and colleagues present the serendipitous discovery of an overdensity of submillimeter galaxies in the field of SDSSJ0909-0108, a post-starburst galaxy at redshift about 0.7. ALMA observations at 870 micrometers and 2 millimeters reveal six objects in a 35 arcsecond region with flux ratios consistent with dust emission. Given the rarity of such sources and ALMA's small field of view, the authors speculate that some sources are physically associated. None share the post-starburst redshift, and four lack spectroscopic redshifts, so follow-up work is suggested to measure redshifts in this potential protocluster.
arxiv-2604-19751: Shintani proposes AI to Learn 2.0, a deliverable-oriented governance framework for judging AI-assisted work in learning-intensive fields, where current rules lag behind fast-moving generative AI. The core problem is proxy failure, where a polished artifact can look useful while no longer proving the human understanding, judgment, or transfer skill the work should build or certify. Rather than claiming piece-by-piece novelty, the framework reorganizes nearby ideas around the final deliverable package and operationalizes them through a five-part package and a seven-dimension maturity rubric.
arxiv-2604-19851: Zilberstein, Martins, and Berker study Condorcet's paradox through automated reasoning with mixed-integer linear programming, the MILP of the title. They consider voters ranking alternatives and committees of chosen alternatives, measuring instability by counting voters who prefer an unchosen alternative to every committee member. A committee counts as a Condorcet winning set when fewer than half the electorate prefers an outsider, though such a set may not exist when the committee size is at most 2.
arxiv-2604-20151: Robertshaw and eight colleagues test a world-model approach for autonomous robotic endovascular intervention, on TD-MPC2. The agent trains on navigation tasks across held-out patient vasculatures and is benchmarked against Soft Actor-Critic, with both validated in vitro on patient phantoms under fluoroscopy. In simulation, TD-MPC2 wins 58 percent to 36 percent over Soft Actor-Critic, with mean tip forces of 0.15 newtons, well below the one-and-a-half-newton rupture threshold. In vitro, TD-MPC2 succeeds 68 percent to 60 percent, wins on path ratios, but takes longer.
arxiv-2604-20251: Zheng studies flocking where members copy a neighbor's heading, lining up or against it. Dice-roll dynamics redraw copy types each step; fixed dynamics lock members in lining-up or lining-against groups. From a microscopic master equation on the circle, Fourier and large-number expansions yield Fokker-Planck equations and random equations for polarization. Rival lining up and lining against wipe out long-range polar order in huge systems, while finite flocks show noise-driven structure set by the mix, as Gillespie runs confirm.
arxiv-2604-20551: Bariletto, Nguyen, Ho, and Rinaldo study Bayesian mixture-of-experts models, with softmax-based gating. They study posterior behavior for three tasks: density estimation, parameter estimation, and model selection. For density estimation they prove posterior contraction rates, with fixed and with random expert numbers. For parameter estimation they derive convergence bounds based on tailored Voronoi-type losses. Finally, they propose and analyze two matching plans for selecting the number of experts. Together, those results give a systematic theory of Bayesian mixture-of-experts models with softmax gating.
arxiv-2604-21851: Arnold and three colleagues develop sequential, anytime-valid tests for stochastic dominance, a notion for comparing distribution functions. Such tests monitor whether one prospect has any upside over another. They derive e-processes against the null that one prospect is dominated by another. For first-order dominance, mixtures of e-variables yield a test of power one valid under ongoing monitoring. The approach extends to higher-order dominance and integral stochastic orders. A baseball application looks at the third-time-through-the-order penalty as a monitoring problem.
arxiv-2604-21951: Bankevich presents a genome assembly model for correct conversion of a read set into an assembly graph under error-free reads. De Bruijn graphs fail to represent read information, while overlap graphs often produce breaks in contigs because contained reads must be discarded first. Bankevich proves a correct form exists in a new class of assembly graphs, called supregraphs. Supregraphs can be built by changing de Bruijn graphs using multiplexing. Under natural assumptions, supregraphs provide a foundation for best genome assemblies.
arxiv-2604-22051: Krause presents int3ract, an R package implementing the Johnson-Neyman technique plus its three-way extension, the Johnson-Neyman-Krause method, for frequentist and Bayesian models. JNK_freq spots models fitted with lm, glm, siena, or lmer and glmer. For two-way interactions, shaded confidence-band plots mark significant and non-significant zones along the moderator range. Three-way interactions produce colour-gradient heatmaps with optional crosshatch shading marking non-significant regions.
arxiv-2604-22451: Alexander and three colleagues prove an integral formula for the spectral flow of smooth loops of unitaries close to the identity in Schatten classes. The formula uses a regularized winding number written with exact differential forms, and it extends from closed loops to open paths. Applied to Schrödinger scattering systems, it yields explicit bound-state counts, adjusted where resonances intrude, in terms of the potential. The paper closes with paths of unbounded operators reached from unitary loops through the Cayley transform, including moving domains and changing Hilbert spaces.
arxiv-2604-22551: Kappel and four colleagues present QDTraj, letting a robot handle many kinds of household objects. Rather than settling for one way to move a hinge or slider, it breeds low-level motion patterns for each task. The search uses quality-diversity methods that explore with sparse rewards. Diversity matters because the best simulated motion may fail amid clutter, so alternatives let the robot pick a fitting pattern. Simulated trajectories were deployed on a real robot, with at least five times more diversity than rival methods on hinge and slider tasks.
arxiv-2604-23051: Atri, Johnson, and Hartvigsen present ChronoScope, a benchmark for temporal consistency in multi-turn language models. It holds over one million Wikidata question chains, testing whether models retain, override, or transfer time-scoped factual context across turns. Tests find temporal scope stability often broken, with models drifting toward present-day beliefs despite correct knowledge. Failures grow with chat length and persist even with oracle context, showing a gap between single-turn factual accuracy and clear reasoning over time.
arxiv-2604-23251: Oliveira and four colleagues study an LLM reviewer built into GitHub pull requests for capstone courses, where review is hard to scale. Across two cohorts of over 100 students, the 2024 group produced far more iterative activity. Failed AI attempts fell from 227 in 2023 to zero after tool and teaching refinements. Responsiveness stayed stable: about one-third of AI-reviewed pull requests drew a follow-up commit in each year. Students used structured AI comments to focus reviews and discuss quality, with guidance curbing over-reliance, yielding recommendations for responsible AI-assisted review.
arxiv-2604-23351: Mehrafarin, Parekh, and Konstas probe whether chain-of-thought tokens carry task information, using activation patching on GSM8K. Moving hidden states from a CoT run into a direct-answer run lifts accuracy above both direct prompting and the trace, even when that trace is wrong. Useful information clusters in middle to late layers and earlier in the trace, with language tokens steering reasoning and maths tokens holding answer-near content. Patched outputs run shorter yet beat full traces, so complete chains are not always needed.
arxiv-2604-23751: Budzinski, Dubach, Féray, Kammoun, and Maïda study Mallows permutations with a bias, conditioned to avoid any length-three pattern. When the bias parameter takes an exponential form in the system size, these permutations converge to an explicit deterministic permuton. The permuton depends on the pattern and the parameter. Along the way they parametrise pattern-avoiding permutons. They prove a large deviation principle for uniform pattern-avoiding permutations. They also estimate two versions of q-Catalan numbers.
arxiv-2604-23851: Ohnishi and Li develop a Bayesian framework for change-plane regression, which sorts patients into two groups by whether a linear score of covariates crosses a threshold. Likelihood inference for the threshold is nonregular. They replace the sharp indicator with a smooth probit gate, treating the smoothed rule as the estimand. At a fixed scale the posterior obeys a Bernstein-von Mises theorem on the rule. Under vanishing smoothing it picks up the boundary faster than the parametric rate allows. Effect inference bears no first-order cost from regularisation.
arxiv-2604-24051: Woo and three colleagues build an unsupervised system for diagnosing anomalies in industrial control systems that run power grids, water plants, and oil and gas sites. Supervised tools need large labeled attack sets, while model-based tools explain little and raise many false alarms. Their framework spots deviations from normal behavior online, then pairs a contextual digital twin with a language model to turn evidence into diagnostic guesses and checks. Tests on public benchmarks show fast, steady, explainable warnings fit for real deployment.
arxiv-2604-24151: Bozga, Iosif, and Zuleger show that recognizable sets of series-parallel graphs admit concise, effective forms via regular grammars. A set counts as recognizable when membership depends only on its image under a homomorphism into a finite algebra, matching what counting monadic second-order logic can define. Their main step builds finite recognizers singly exponential in grammar size, down from double exponential. Intersection and inclusion for such sets then become EXPTIME-complete, beating a prior 2EXPTIME bound.
arxiv-2604-24251: Han and colleagues describe the Science User Support Services at the SVOM Chinese Science Center. SVOM studies gamma-ray bursts from the distant universe. SUSS backs its science operations with two pillars: specialized software that automates key workflows, and a human team offering coordination, technical help, training, and problem-solving across the observation lifecycle. The paper details the General Platform, Burst Advocate tools for counterpart identification, Target of Opportunity tools, and General Program tools, plus team structure. A first-year evaluation judges how well user needs were met.
arxiv-2604-24351: Duan, Zhang, and Chen present Diffusion Templates, a plugin framework splitting inference from capability injection. Solo systems with clashing lines and hooks make reuse, transfer, and mixing hard. The framework has three parts: Template models mapping inputs to capability forms, a Template cache, and a Template pipeline. The pipeline loads, merges, and injects caches. The systems-level link lets carriers such as KV-Cache and LoRA work under one idea. A model zoo spans shape control, brightness, color, editing, super-detail, sharpness, looks, guide, fill-in, and age control.
arxiv-2604-25051: Bacher maps the semigroup tree to find Eliahou semigroups of conductor up to 200. A new semigroup coding plus pruning makes the search work, hoped up to 400. This proves Wilf's conjecture for conductors up to 200. From the list, he describes new semigroup classes with a Farey interval. He shows these semigroups likely all satisfy Wilf's conjecture. He constructs families of Eliahou semigroups in these classes, alongside families from Bras-Amorós and from Delgado, Eliahou and Fromentin.
arxiv-2604-25151: Rivin proves a short rigidity result for Lambert series. If a sequence repeats by a linear rule after some point and its Lambert series is rational, then only finitely many of its terms are nonzero. So among sequences with a rational ordinary generating function, only finitely supported ones give a rational Lambert series.
